# Changelog

Every release note, newest first. Each links to the full note in
`docs/release-notes/`.

**This file is generated.** Add a note to the directory, then run
`node scripts/changelog.mjs`; `--check` refuses a stale one in `verify`.

- [`0.1.1`](docs/release-notes/0.1.1.md) — Documentation only. No code changed, and nothing needs upgrading.
- [`0.1.0`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0.md) — The wire is locked. What that means, and what it deliberately does not.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.103`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.103.md) — Three results that a device produced and a site never showed.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.102`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.102.md) — A hosted console was landing in `/bin/sh`. There is no default now.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.101`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.101.md) — The box greets an empty room. Whoever arrives now hears it.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.100`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.100.md) — `0.1.0-alpha.99` shipped the console's shared codec through one door. The browser comes in the other one.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.99`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.99.md) — The console dropped every keystroke's echo. Two ends, two base64 alphabets.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.98`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.98.md) — The box signs its console data connection. It never has.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.97`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.97.md) — The box now opens its console control socket. It never has before.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.96`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.96.md) — The console listener stays up, and `onNoRunner` accepts the handler its own documentation promised.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.95`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.95.md) — A door into the protocol that a browser can walk through.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.94`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.94.md) — `byollm services manage` now shows you what your CLIs actually serve, instead of asking you to remember.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.93`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.93.md) — A job that timed out could leave a helper process behind, and the console protocol arrives.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.92`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.92.md) — A daemon started by a supervisor no longer waits for an answer nobody can give.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.91`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.91.md) — A chat message is picked up when it arrives, not up to ten seconds later.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.90`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.90.md) — `byollm status` now tells you whether the daemon is actually running.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.89`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.89.md) — The largest single message byollm carries is now 6 MB, down from 10.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.88`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.88.md) — byollm now starts a local model server when a job needs one.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.87`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.87.md) — Your device stops offering a model server that is not running.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.58`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.58.md) — `alpha.58` — sites declare what they need; they no longer name what runs it.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.52`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.52.md) — `alpha.52` — a device that is running and invisible now says so, and `byollm offer` no longer disagrees wit...
- [`0.1.0-alpha.51`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.51.md) — `alpha.51` makes service selection actually work.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.50`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.50.md) — `alpha.50` — the background daemon can find your CLIs. Reinstall the service after upgrading:
- [`0.1.0-alpha.49`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.49.md) — `alpha.49` fixes what the wizard writes, and makes `enqueue` refuse options it does not understand.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.48`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.48.md) — `alpha.48` finishes service selection through the SDK.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.47`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.47.md) — `alpha.47` adds `byollm setup` and the Codex CLI.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.46`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.46.md) — `alpha.46` lets a site name a service.
- [`0.1.0-alpha.45`](docs/release-notes/0.1.0-alpha.45.md) — `alpha.45` carries withheld kinds on the heartbeat.
